chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Bakr Al-Hazrami, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'My wife permitted her slave girl to me.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Marry her if you wish.' I said, 'Can I sell her?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No, rather it is permitted to you from her whatever she has permitted.'

key_terms.أَحَلَّتْ: Permitted/allowed (specifically in the context of making a slave girl permissible for marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a wife permitting her slave girl to her husband for marriage versus for ownership?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between granting the right of marriage (nikah) versus ownership (tamlik) when a wife permits her slave girl to her husband. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that the permission is limited to the marital bond, thereby preventing the husband from selling the girl as he would with his own property. This ruling highlights the precise legal boundaries of usufruct rights within the family structure in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘My wife permitted her slave girl to me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Marry her if you so want’. I said, ‘Can I sell her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but rather it is Permitted to you from her whatever she has permitted’.
